title: Functoriality of the derived Mayer--Vietoris triangle
statement:
Let W be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] with W=U\cup V, U and V quasi-compact open subschemes, and open immersions j_U, j_V, j_{UV}. For E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W) [def-pc-derived-category] write MV(E) for the distinguished triangle E\to R(j_U)_*E|_U\oplus R(j_V)_*E|_V\to R(j_{UV})_*E|_{U\cap V}\xrightarrow{\delta_E}E[1] of [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-triangle] [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Choose a K-injective complex \mathcal I^\bullet representing E whose terms are injective [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open] its restrictions are K-injective, and \delta_E is the boundary morphism that [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] attaches to the degreewise short exact sequence 0\to\mathcal I^\bullet\to j_{U,*}(\mathcal I^\bullet|_U)\oplus j_{V,*}(\mathcal I^\bullet|_V)\to j_{UV,*}(\mathcal I^\bullet|_{U\cap V})\to0, which is exact because the restriction maps of the injective modules \mathcal I^n are surjective [lem-sc-ringed-space-injective-restriction-surjective]. Then:
(1) (naturality in E) for every morphism \varphi:E\to F in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W), the triple (\varphi,\ R(j_U)_*(\varphi|_U)\oplus R(j_V)_*(\varphi|_V),\ R(j_{UV})_*(\varphi|_{U\cap V})) is a morphism of distinguished triangles MV(E)\to MV(F); in particular \varphi[1]\circ\delta_E=\delta_F\circ R(j_{UV})_*(\varphi|_{U\cap V}).
(2) (compatibility with direct image) let h:W'\to W be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes, put U'=h^{-1}(U), V'=h^{-1}(V), assume W' quasi-compact and quasi-separated and U', V' quasi-compact, and let E'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{W'}), so that Rh_*E'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_W) [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh]. Then Rh_* applied to MV(E') for the cover W'=U'\cup V' is a distinguished triangle in D(\mathcal O_W), and the canonical isomorphisms Rh_*R(j_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'})\cong R(j_T)_*R(h|_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'})\cong R(j_T)_*((Rh_*E')|_T) for T\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}, T'=h^{-1}(T) [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition], together with the identity of Rh_*E', form an isomorphism of distinguished triangles Rh_*MV(E')\cong MV(Rh_*E'), compatible with the connecting morphisms Rh_*(\delta_{E'}) and \delta_{Rh_*E'}. The composition comparisons in clause (2) are normalized by their right-derived unit equation, and the open-restriction comparison is the derived sectionwise identity. Their data are those of [def-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-canonical-data], not arbitrary isomorphisms selected from Nonempty.

proof.text: Implemented clause (1): choose the functorial K-injective resolution with injective terms of a complex representing each derived object, and transport its localization back to that object. Fix the derived open restriction adjunctions. The concrete Mayer--Vietoris complex of def-pc-kinjective-mayer-vietoris-data is short exact by lem-pc-kinjective-mayer-vietoris-exact. Define the boundary using triangleOfSESδ and the inverse explicitly constructed intersection comparison of def-pc-open-image-complex-comparison-iso. The unit and nested restriction identities from lem-pc-open-image-complex-comparison-unit and lem-pc-open-image-complex-comparison-restriction, together with the localization biproduct comparison, give an isomorphism from triangleOfSES to the required triangle, proving distinguishedness. Represent every derived morphism between the resolutions by a chain map using lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison and fullness of the homotopy quotient. This chain map gives a morphism of the concrete short exact sequences. Naturality of the right-derived computation isomorphism gives naturality of the explicit intersection comparison. triangleOfSESδ_naturality from lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle then gives the boundary square. Transport through the two resolution isomorphisms. The first square is naturality of the adjunction units, and the second applies Mathlib NatTrans.naturality to the locally assembled scheme restriction natural transformation; its components reduce to the adjunction mate by Adjunction.homEquiv_unit. No separate generic mate-naturality theorem is declared. These three squares construct the triangle morphism with exactly the required components. This argument works for all derived objects, so the quasi-coherent hypotheses are not needed for this clause. Clause (2) is reduced to the two comparison obligations in the next steps.

proof.text: Construct the fixed K-injective boundary families and derived restriction adjunctions of def-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-canonical-data. The existing representativeBoundary_naturality and representativeBoundary_distinguished proofs show that these exact families are natural and their triangles distinguished (canonicalMV_spec). Quasi-coherence of Rh_*E follows from schemeDerivedDirectImage_preserves_QCoh, and the image triangle is distinguished by the triangulated right-derived functor. The private transport_boundary_square proves the transport algebra abstractly; explicit universe parameters in canonicalMV_spec calls fix the derived-category universe and avoid unconstrained instance searches.

The first two equations of lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-direct-image-squares and the separate boundary equation of lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-direct-image-boundary supply exactly the three inputs to Triangle.isoMk. Use identity on the first object, the additive biproduct comparison on the middle object, and the intersection comparison on the third. The explicitly composed open isomorphisms have the stipulated normalized components by reflexivity; biprod.hom_ext and mapBiprod_hom prove the formula for the middle component. Bind the square conjunction as a named fact and project its two equations to preserve comparison transparency during elaboration. The private boundary_square_identity proves the shift-of-identity algebra abstractly before applying it to the scheme boundary.

old_proof.text: Choose a K-injective complex \mathcal I'^\bullet with injective terms representing E' and a K-injective complex \mathcal J^\bullet with injective terms representing Rh_*E', together with a quasi-isomorphism q:h_*\mathcal I'^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Apply the triangulated functor Rh_* to the distinguished triangle MV(E') [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. For T\in\{U,V,U\cap V\} restrict q to T and apply j_{T,*}. Since (h_*\mathcal I'^\bullet)|_T=h_{T',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'}) (elementary), the source is j_{T,*}h_{T',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'})=h_*j_{T',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'}), which represents Rh_*R(j_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'})\cong R(j_T)_*R(h_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'}) [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] because \mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'} is K-injective [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open]; the target j_{T,*}(\mathcal J^\bullet|_T) represents R(j_T)_*((Rh_*E')|_T), and q|_T realizes the isomorphism R(h_{T'})_*(E'|_{T'})\cong(Rh_*E')|_T of [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. Thus these components give the asserted isomorphisms on the second and third terms, while the first term is identified by the identity of Rh_*E'.

source.place: Tag 0DJ9 induction step, identification of relative Mayer--Vietoris terms after derived direct-image composition

old_proof.text: The sequence 0\to\mathcal I'^\bullet\to j_{U',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{U'})\oplus j_{V',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{V'})\to j_{U'V',*}(\mathcal I'^\bullet|_{U'\cap V'})\to0 defining MV(E') is split in every degree because each \mathcal I'^n is injective (elementary). Its terms are K-injective: \mathcal I'^\bullet|_{T'} by [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open], its image under j_{T',*} because j_{T',*} is right adjoint to the exact restriction functor [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], and a finite direct sum of K-injective complexes is K-injective (elementary). Hence [lem-pc-derived-functor-termwise-split-ses-triangle] applied to F=h_* identifies Rh_*MV(E'), including Rh_*(\delta_{E'}), with the triangle of the image sequence 0\to h_*\mathcal I'^\bullet\to\cdots\to0. The map q of Step 2 and its restrictions give a morphism of short exact sequences from this image sequence to the sequence defining MV(Rh_*E') with the representative \mathcal J^\bullet, whose components are the isomorphisms of Step 2. The naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] applied to this morphism gives Q(q)[1]\circ Rh_*(\delta_{E'})=\delta_{Rh_*E'}\circ(\text{the intersection-term isomorphism}). Thus the three component isomorphisms form an isomorphism of distinguished triangles Rh_*MV(E')\cong MV(Rh_*E'), compatible with the connecting morphisms.
